SpiderPi is a Raspberry Pi-powered AI vision hexapod robot from Hiwonder with three servos per leg (18 DOF), a 2-DOF wide-angle camera and an 11.1 V 2,500 mAh lithium battery. It is used for teaching Python programming, machine vision and legged locomotion.

JetRover is a composite ROS education robot from Hiwonder offered with Mecanum-wheel, Ackermann or tank chassis and powered by NVIDIA Jetson or Raspberry Pi. ROSpider is an all-terrain ROS 2 hexapod platform from Hiwonder with eighteen 35 kg high-voltage bus servos, a 6-DOF robotic arm with gripper, LiDAR, a 3D depth camera, a six-microphone array and an OLED display, running on Jetson or Raspberry Pi. It supports SLAM mapping and navigation, 3D grasping and multimodal large AI models, powered by an 11.1 V 6,000 mAh battery.

AiMecha M1 is an AI educational robot car from Hiwonder with an all-metal Mecanum-wheel chassis, a 3-DOF vision robotic arm, an ESP32 + MM32 dual-core controller and the K230-based WonderLens Pro AI module with a 1080p camera and 2.4-inch touchscreen. It offers more than 30 offline vision functions, connects to large language models such as DeepSeek, Doubao and Qwen, and is programmable in Scratch and MicroPython.

ROSOrin is a ROS 2 multimodal AI robot car from Hiwonder with a modular aluminum chassis that switches between Mecanum, Ackermann and four-wheel differential drive. ROSMASTER A1 is a ROS 2 educational robot car from Yahboom with an Ackermann steering chassis and AI large-language-model integration.

Kamigami are app-controlled, fold-together six-legged robot kits from Dash Robotics, a UC Berkeley spin-off, introduced in 2015. They use infrared, accelerometer and gyroscope sensors, run about 60 minutes per charge and sold for around 50 USD; the line is discontinued.

Viam Rover 2 is a preassembled two-wheel-drive development rover from New York-based Viam for learning and prototyping with the Viam robotics software platform, introduced in 2023. It has encoded motors with suspension, a 720p webcam with microphone, a 6-DoF IMU and power-monitoring electronics on an aluminum chassis that carries up to 20 lb; a Raspberry Pi 4 and batteries are bought separately.

The original TurtleBot is a low-cost, open-source ROS mobile robot developed at Willow Garage and released in 2011, combining an iRobot Create base, a Microsoft Kinect 3D sensor and an Asus netbook. It could build maps, navigate autonomously and detect people and objects, and sold for about 1,500 USD assembled; TurtleBot 1 and 2 are discontinued.

Small educational humanoid robot from Wuhan-based Guanggu Shengchuang, first launched at WRC 2026. It is about 40 cm tall with 18 joint degrees of freedom, has built-in large-language-model voice interaction and a graded programming curriculum, and targets home companionship and K-12 AI education.

Open-source whole-body teleoperation platform from AgileX Robotics (松灵机器人) based on Stanford's Mobile ALOHA architecture. It combines a TRACER 2.0 mobile base with four 6-DOF PiPER arms (two leader, two follower), wrist and top-view cameras and an onboard PC for bimanual manipulation, demonstration-data collection and VLA model training.

Dual-arm teleoperation platform from AgileX Robotics built on the RANGER MINI 3.0 omnidirectional base with four PiPER 6-DOF arms, three depth cameras, a LiDAR and an RTX 4060 industrial computer. Its split leader-follower design allows cross-space remote teleoperation and adjustable working height for embodied-AI data collection; it was added to AgileX's lineup in July 2026.

Compact four-wheel-drive, four-wheel-steering omnidirectional base from AgileX Robotics designed to carry humanoid upper bodies, dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators for embodied-AI research. It supports lateral movement and zero-radius turns, has a 25 km full-load range and offers CAN, C++ SDK and ROS/ROS 2 interfaces.

Grizzly is an ATV-sized, all-electric robotic utility vehicle from Clearpath Robotics for agriculture, mining and defence research, unveiled in March 2013. It has four independently driven wheels with 26-inch tyres and a passive oscillating front axle, a 600 kg payload, 6300 N (1400 lbf) drawbar pull, a single-point Class 1 hitch, up to 19 km/h and about 12 hours of basic run time, with ROS, C++ and MathWorks interfaces.

Meccanoid G15 is a build-it-yourself programmable robot kit sold under Spin Master's Meccano brand, launched in spring 2015 as the smaller sibling of the G15 KS. The 615-piece, 61 cm robot uses servo motors and the Meccabrain controller, supports voice recognition and LIM (learned intelligent movement) recording of poses demonstrated by hand, and sold for about 200 EUR in France.

Meccanoid G15 KS (King Size) is a 1,223-piece, 122 cm programmable humanoid robot kit from Spin Master's Meccano brand, shown at CES 2015 and shipped from October 2015. It has eight servo motors, voice recognition with thousands of phrases, LIM (learned intelligent movement) recording and an open-source Meccabrain platform; the full kit was priced at 400 USD (360 EUR in France).

Interactive STEM robot for children aged 4 to 12 from WhalesBot that can be played with directly, driven with a controller or programmed through the Pubbo app, which provides lessons, missions and online competitions. It has multiple sensors and expressive displays.

Updated version of the Montessori-inspired Cubetto wooden coding robot for children aged 3 and up, programmed screen-free by placing 24 coding blocks on an interface board with an 18-step main sequence plus a 4-step function line. It adds left-to-right program order and USB-C rechargeable batteries rated for about 2 hours of robot play and 10 hours on the board; sold by Primo Toys, now operated by Moravia Consulting in Brno.

Wooden screen-free coding robot for children aged 3 and up, created by London-based Primo Toys, that is programmed with tangible coding blocks on an interface board and drives across an illustrated map. Its 2016 Kickstarter raised about 1.6 million USD and it won a Red Dot Best of the Best award in 2016.

Origin One is a modular, ROS 2-programmable ground robot platform made by Dutch company Avular for autonomous research and development missions. It carries a 30 kg payload up to 10 km on a charge, runs an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX for navigation and obstacle avoidance, and supports add-ons such as a Kinova Gen3 arm, mecanum wheels and an RTK GNSS base station.

Leka is a small, ball-shaped interactive robot made by French company Leka for therapists and educators working with children with autism and other disabilities. It uses an expressive face display, colored lights, vibration and RFID-readable "magic cards" to deliver sensory stimulation and learning activities, and charges by induction on a docking base.

Robotino is an omnidirectional mobile robot platform made by Festo Didactic (part of German automation company Festo) for education, training and research. It drives on three independently controlled Mecanum wheels arranged 120 degrees apart for unrestricted movement, connects over WLAN, and can be programmed in C++, Java or MATLAB as well as with Festo's own software for autonomous navigation exercises.

Mobile FR3 Duo is a research robot platform from German robotics maker Franka Robotics that integrates its dual-arm Franka Research 3 Duo manipulator system with an omnidirectional mobile base called the Tactile Mobile Robot (TMR), combining dual-arm manipulation and mobility for physical AI research such as teleoperation, dataset collection and policy execution outside fixed workcells. Announced as part of Franka's upcoming Physical AI reference platform lineup, it is available to research customers via early access as of late 2026.

STEM Coding Max is a construction and coding robotics kit from German maker Fischertechnik aimed at secondary-school students, built around an RX controller with gesture, color, proximity and brightness sensors, two XS motors and touch sensors. Using block- and text-based programming through the companion STEM Suite app, students build 11 base models (plus 4 bonus models) from its 243 parts to complete everyday information-technology and robotics tasks.

STEM Coding Ultimate AI is an upper-secondary robotics and artificial-intelligence construction kit from German maker Fischertechnik, built around its TXT 4.0 controller, a USB camera, ultrasonic and track sensors, and encoder motors. Students program 12 expandable models with Blockly or Python and use an included software tool to train simple neural networks for tasks such as object recognition and automated decision-making.

Thymio 3 is the next-generation version of the open-source Thymio educational robot, designed with EPFL and ECAL and produced by the Swiss nonprofit Mobsya, succeeding the earlier Thymio II (now sold as Thymio 2+). It adds built-in Bluetooth (replacing the old USB dongle), a 3-axis gyroscope and accelerometer for precise geometric movement, a ground-facing RGB color sensor, an audio chip for recording and MP3 playback, and USB-C charging with 3 to 6 hours of runtime, programmed through the thymio.lab coding platform. Pre-orders opened in July 2026 for classroom delivery that September.

e.DO is a small, open-source 6-axis educational robot arm made by Italian automation company Comau for teaching robotics, mathematics and programming. It has 6 powered axes, a 1 kg maximum payload, and a modular design that supports pick-and-place exercises and multiple programming languages.

The ROBBO Kit is a comprehensive robot construction kit for STEAM education, built with magnetic-mount sensors and an LED light so students can assemble and program their own robot. It is one of several hardware products from Robbo, a Russian-founded educational robotics company with international subsidiaries including in Finland and Japan.

The ROBBO Dancing Robot is an interactive robot-friend from educational robotics company Robbo that can walk, dance, make sounds or play melodies, and avoid obstacles, designed as an entry point for students into robotics and technology.

KOOV is a robotics and programming learning kit from Sony Global Education built around colorful building blocks, electronic parts and a companion app for visual block-based coding. The Advance Kit is the top tier of Sony's four KOOV kits (Entry, Basic 2, Starter and Advance), bundling the largest set of blocks and electronic parts for open-ended builds, priced at 64,800 JPY. KOOV has won awards including the iF Design Award 2017 and the Japan e-Learning Award, and Sony continues to run recurring KOOV design contests for students.

IRIS is a wheeled humanoid AI tutor robot with a chest-mounted screen and speakers, developed by South African company BSG and Technologies (founded by Bonisiwe "Thandoh" Gumede) in partnership with Indian robotics firm MakerLabs, and publicly launched in Durban in August 2025. It uses natural language processing, voice interaction and adaptive learning to teach subjects from Grade R through tertiary level in all 11 of South Africa's official languages. As of August 2026 it was running in five KwaZulu-Natal schools on donated units, with parts cut in India and assembled at Durban's Dube TradePort; the national science department has publicly endorsed the project but has not funded it.

Ubuntu-12 is a 3D-printed robotic arm made by Kenyan startup ZeroBionic, founded by Norah Kimathi, that translates a teacher's spoken STEM lessons into sign language for deaf students in real time and uses computer vision to read students' signing back into text. Printed largely from recycled plastic, each unit costs about 350 USD, works offline, and the company reports roughly 92 percent speech-to-sign translation accuracy across more than 150 classroom pilots in Africa.

Cuma is a humanoid-shaped (head, torso and arms) robotic-coding education robot made by Turkish company Biorobotec, built as the first stage of its robotics program before the humanoid Tomyris. It can distinguish between men, women, children and adults facing it and mimics the hand and facial movements of the person it is interacting with as part of coding and robotics lessons.

The AMZ S1 is a 95 cm tall humanoid classroom robot made by AMZ AI Robotics (Grupo Realms) in Manaus, Brazil, with a chest-mounted tablet, depth camera and 9-axis IMU for autonomous navigation. It runs local AI models of up to 7 billion parameters to teach English and programming (Python, ROS 2, block coding), support reading practice and communicate with autistic students via pictograms. Announced in 2026 with a Manaus production line targeting 200 units in its first year; first deliveries are planned for mid-2027.
